correspondences.notes: BIDS has no visual-field or microperimetry suffix.

brainlife.desc: Microperimetry (fundus-controlled perimetry, e.g. MAIA) retinal sensitivity per test point as a TSV: ID, x_deg, y_deg, Threshold.
brainlife.name: neuro/microperimetry

original.desc: Microperimetry or fundus-controlled perimetry provides an evaluation of visual function by testing the visual field with incorporated eye-tracking. [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33022378/]. This app is optimised for use on binocular integrated data produced by  https://ocular.shinyapps.io/MAIA_binocular_field_app/
original.readme:
Example microperimetry.tsv

* File will be read as "space delimited" in validator and then converted to a proper tsv (tab delimited) files

```
"ID"  "x_deg"   "y_deg"   "Threshold"
69  -9.04   -0.61   28
62  -8.95   1.39    28
59  -7.21   -4.69   26
```

Full record: https://github.com/brainlife/abcd-spec/blob/master/datatypes/neuro.microperimetry.json

files.desc: A tab-separated values (TSV) file containing 4 columns (ID, x_deg, y_deg, and Threshold") and sets of values.

identifying_risks: Rare retinal conditions in small samples.
governance.rationale: Tool 1 step 6: participant-level clinical vision data; step 8 for rare conditions.
sharing_cautions: Remove exam dates and device patient IDs before sharing.
tier_conditions: Tier 3 if linked to names or exam dates in the export.

inputs_of.name: MAIA microperimetry analysis
inputs_of.purpose: eccentricity-ring averages of MAIA retinal sensitivity

intended_use: Ring-wise retinal sensitivity summaries with the MAIA analysis App.
not_suitable_for: Space-delimited exports without conversion to TSV.
